scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Hot tea stays hot for hours, and cold water stays cold. How does a thermos know which one you want?

scenes.name: three
scenes.text: It doesn't know. It just blocks heat moving at all. Heat travels in three ways: conduction, convection and radiation.

scenes.name: vacuum
scenes.text: A thermos has two walls with a vacuum between them. With almost no air, conduction and convection nearly stop.

scenes.name: shiny
scenes.text: The walls are shiny, which reflects infrared radiation back, instead of letting it escape.

scenes.name: lid
scenes.text: The lid is the weak spot. A tight, insulated stopper keeps warm air from escaping at the top.

scenes.name: both
scenes.text: Since it slows heat in either direction, it keeps cold drinks cold just as well.

scenes.name: tip
scenes.text: Pre-fill it with hot water for a minute first, so the inner wall doesn't steal heat from your tea.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Vacuum, shiny walls, tight lid. Heat has nowhere to go. Follow for more on how things really work.
